title: McDonough District Hospital announces new board chair following leadership changes
text:
Jere Greuel Chairman | McDonough District Hospital
Jere Greuel Chairman | McDonough District Hospital
During the January meeting of the McDonough District Hospital (MDH) Board of Directors, Jere Greuel announced his decision to step down as Board Chair while remaining a member of the board. The meeting took place on January 19 in Macomb, Illinois.
Dan O’Neill was unanimously elected to move from Vice Chair to Board Chair. JoEllen Pensinger was also unanimously chosen as Vice Chair. Ryan Riggins will continue serving as Secretary/Treasurer.
President and Chief Executive Officer Bill Murdock commented on the leadership transition: “Working with Jere Greuel over the past two years to fulfill his vision for the future of MDH has been rewarding and meaningful. His interaction with staff and leadership has been impactful to rebuilding the culture of MDH,” said Murdock. “Congratulations to our incoming Board Chair Dan O’Neill. His leadership as a business owner and community icon will help take MDH to the next level. I am looking forward to working closely with Dan as we continue to improve the experience of delivering excellent patient care at MDH and continue to strategically grow our hospital.”
Greuel joined the board in February 2018, became Vice Chair in January 2022, and served as Chair starting in 2023. He is currently the longest-serving member on the board.
O’Neill became a board member in January 2019 and was selected as Vice Chair four years later. Pensinger joined the board in January 2024.
At this meeting, Shane Miller, PharmD, Supervisor at MDH Community Pharmacy, provided an update on pharmacy operations. The pharmacy marked its one-year anniversary on January 15. Miller reported that prescription volumes have increased steadily, reaching record numbers for both monthly totals and single-day fills. “Average daily totals are now equal to what the daily records were two months ago. The Community Pharmacy is continuing to adjust staffing and workflow to meet patient needs,” Miller said.
